If Simoon is Normal Summoned, Black Whirlwind searches Sudri (or another Blackwing under 1600 ATK), and I still keep my own Normal Summon. That is the start of the main line. Sending Simoon to the GY instead throws the whole engine away.

positions.assessment: Chinook can respond here as a Quick Effect because BWD is on the field, and it would negate Witch's search. That trades Chinook (plus a spare Synchro from the Extra Deck) one-for-one against an unknown Forbidden Quick-Play. But Chinook on the field is the Blackwing that lets Vata Special Summon on my turn: Vata + BWD makes Full Armor Master, and Chinook is also a DARK Tribute for Ahrima. Saffira's End Phase effect (random discard from my hand or draw 2) is at least as good a target for a once-per-turn negate. Keeping Chinook keeps all of those options open.

grades.label: B
grades.reason: The rules are right: Chinook can negate the search mid-chain. But it spends Chinook on a minor one-for-one, gives up the field Blackwing that Vata needs on my turn, and loses the chance to answer Saffira's stronger End Phase effect.

positions.assessment: The real choice is to finish the Lv8 Synchro with Nothung + Sharnga or to cancel. If I Synchro, the opponent gets another Maxx "C" draw, my two bodies become one, and my GY grows to 4 DARK monsters. That makes Dark Armed Dragon (which needs exactly 3) essentially dead. It also strands Sharnga's GY effect unless I later control a Blackwing Synchro, since BWD, Void Ogre and Omega aren't Blackwing Synchros. If I keep Nothung + Sharnga, then once Sharnga dies the GY holds exactly 3 DARK monsters, which turns on Dark Armed Dragon, and Sharnga's quick destroy is live while Nothung stays out. Cancelling looks better.

grades.label: A
grades.reason: The reason only looks at the stats of the bigger body. It ignores the extra Maxx "C" draw, that the GY going to 4 DARK makes Dark Armed Dragon unusable, and that Sharnga's GY effect only works with a Blackwing Synchro on the field.
